title: Let a workflow definition customize a delivery orchestration's required role stages
description:
internal/workflowdef already models exactly the reusable-pattern concept discussed while scoping punokawan-14yn.10's ceremonial-surface removal: a versioned, invokable Definition with per-role restrictions (Definition.Roles[role].Required/Mode/Capabilities) that can reduce a role's participation. Today nothing in internal/delivery consults this - RecordRoleStage/CompleteLease's role-stage gate is hardcoded to require all four of Semar/Gareng/Petruk/Bagong once a lane opts in (rolestage.go), with no way to invoke a lighter variant (e.g. skip Petruk planning for a trivial hotfix, or require an extra independent Bagong pass for a high-risk change) without hand-waving past the gate entirely.

Design: add an optional workflow_definition_id to DeliveryOrchestration (or DeliveryLane), settable at start_delivery/create_orchestration time and validated against workflowdef's store (must exist and be enabled). RecordRoleStage/CompleteLease look up the referenced Definition's Roles map (when present) to decide which stages are actually required for that lane's gate, falling back to today's all-four-required behavior when no definition is attached - existing callers with no definition see zero behavior change. workflowdef.Invoker's RunCreator gets a real, meaningful implementation for the first time: invoking a delivery-shaped definition translates its inputs into a StartDelivery call carrying the definition's id, so a saved pattern becomes 'start a delivery this way' rather than the old single-project workflow run it currently creates. Definition.Steps (the general capability-DAG) is not literally executed for these invocations - a delivery-oriented definition mainly uses Roles/AllowedCapabilities/ApprovalPolicy as a configuration overlay, since the delivery domain's own fixed lane/lease/role-stage sequence is the thing actually running, not an arbitrary step graph.

Boundary: Definition.Steps continues to be executed via the existing internal/workflow run engine for non-delivery-shaped definitions (e.g. pure Jira/Slack automation with no code change involved) - this task does not touch that path, only adds a second, delivery-aware RunCreator variant chosen by the definition's own shape (a definition with a non-empty Roles map and no Steps that map to non-delivery capabilities is delivery-shaped; ambiguous cases should fail closed with a clear error asking the definition to be explicit, not guess).
acceptance_criteria: 1. A saved workflow definition with Roles={gareng:{required:false},petruk:{required:false}} attached to a delivery orchestration lets CompleteLease succeed once only Semar+Bagong are recorded, without weakening the gate for any lane with no definition attached. 2. Invoking such a definition via the existing invoke path calls StartDelivery and returns a real orchestration id, not a legacy workflow run id. 3. A definition referencing a nonexistent or disabled id is rejected at attach time, not silently ignored. 4. Every existing rolestage.go/scheduler_test.go test with no definition attached keeps passing unmodified - this is additive, not a behavior change for the default path. 5. workflowdef's own existing tests (invoke_test.go, resolve_test.go, validation_test.go) keep passing unmodified.
close_reason: All 5 acceptance criteria met (commit 4971a25). DeliveryOrchestration carries an optional workflow_definition_id, validated exists+enabled at CreateOrchestrationWithDefinition time via an injected WorkflowDefinitionResolver (internal/delivery/workflowdefinition.go) - no import cycle to internal/workflowdef, decoupled anyway since the two packages own unrelated persistence lifecycles. CompleteLease's role-stage gate resolves required stages per-definition (absent role/empty Roles map/no definition all mean required - only explicit Required:false disables a stage), verified against a lane with gareng+petruk marked optional succeeding on Semar+Bagong alone, a lane with an empty Roles map still requiring all four, and every pre-existing no-definition test passing unmodified. invoke_workflow_definition gives workflowdef's Invoker a real second RunCreator: a Roles-bearing definition now starts an actual delivery orchestration instead of a legacy workflow run; a Roles-empty definition keeps using the untouched legacy path. internal/workflowdef itself has zero diff.

title: punakawan panel leaves an orphaned dolt sql-server child process on exit
description: After stopping 'punakawan panel' (e.g. Ctrl-C), the per-project dolt sql-server child process it spawned for .punakawan/knowledge can survive as an orphan (PPID reparented to 1) instead of being terminated. Observed directly: PID 40208, started by an earlier punakawan panel run, still bound to this repo's .punakawan/knowledge with no living parent - it blocked 'punakawan knowledge hub migrate' with ErrLegacyServerRunning until manually killed. Likely cause: the dolt sql-server subprocess isn't in the same process group / isn't explicitly terminated in the panel's shutdown path (cmd/punakawan/panel_cmd.go's signal.NotifyContext + s.Shutdown), so a SIGINT to the parent doesn't propagate to it, or app.Close doesn't wait for/kill the underlying dolt server process.
acceptance_criteria: Starting and then stopping 'punakawan panel' (SIGINT/SIGTERM) leaves no dolt sql-server process running for that project afterward. Verify by checking 'ps' for a dolt sql-server bound to the project's data dir immediately after the panel process exits.
close_reason: Root cause eliminated by punokawan-14yn.15: internal/knowledge no longer starts a dolt sql-server at all (Open/OpenInHub and the whole Dolt-backed Store were replaced by the shared SQLite kernel). Verified: no runtime code path spawns 'dolt sql-server' anymore (grep-confirmed), full test suite passes with no dolt binary present.

title: Fix /api/v1/events duration_ms logging: SSE connection lifetime logged as processing time
description: loggingMiddleware measures time.Since(start) after next.ServeHTTP returns, for every route. The SSE handler blocks in an infinite loop until client disconnect, so its duration_ms is the connection's open duration (seen: 28s-94s), not real processing time - misleading in logs, looks like a performance bug. Special-case the SSE route (or move connection-open/close logging into SSEHandler itself) so duration_ms reflects real work.
close_reason: loggingMiddleware now detects a text/event-stream response and logs it as 'panel stream closed' with connection_duration_ms, instead of misrepresenting SSE connection lifetime as duration_ms processing time. Tested in internal/panel/server/server_test.go.

title: Parallelize gitHealth's per-repo git status shellouts
description: workspace_source.go's gitHealth loops sequentially over every repo in a workspace, one git status shellout each. WorkspaceSource.List and describe() already use a bounded semaphore-channel + WaitGroup pattern (maxConcurrent=4) for this exact kind of fan-out - reuse it here instead of inventing a new one.
close_reason: gitHealth now fans out one git status per repo through the same bounded worker pool (max 4 concurrent) already used by List/describe, instead of a sequential per-repo loop. Order-preserving (results assembled by index, not append). 1 new test (20 repeated runs, -race clean), full repo suite green.

title: session_source.go counts(): read persisted sessionsummary.yaml before rescanning ledger/journal
description: sessionsummary.WriteYAML already persists per-run EvidenceCount/WarningCount/ErrorCount to .punakawan/runs/<runID>/summary.yaml right after a checkpoint advance (session_source.go's WriteSessionSummary hook), but nothing reads it back - counts() always rescans the full ledger+journal file per run. Make counts() prefer sessionsummary.ReadYAML and only fall back to a live scan when the summary file is missing (older runs predating this feature) or the run is still active (summary may be stale mid-run).
notes: Deferred: benefits sessions-list/detail pages, not overview (overview no longer calls counts() at all - see z7no's SkipCounts). Overview was the user's actual complaint; this is a secondary win with real staleness-safety design work needed (active vs terminal runs) - not urgent.

Safe because dolt data is on disk and restarts on demand.

title: Phase 4: add reviewed learning
description: Extend artifact types with workflow/project-metadata/knowledge; three typed artifact adapters (validate + write immutable revision, never auto-activate/promote). propose_project_learning + deterministic fingerprint dedup (workflow: scope+selector+normalized step graph; metadata: scope+normalized key; knowledge: scope+type+subject+source hash). Panel Context Improvements inbox reusing existing review UI. On acceptance, update canonical store+search index+audit atomically from caller view; keep workflow acceptance vs activation separate. EXIT: proposal can't alter canon pre-acceptance; stale-base acceptance -> readable conflict; equivalent observations update one pending proposal; accepted improvement selected by next prepare_work_context.
close_reason: Phase 4 done: 3 typed artifact adapters (workflow/metadata/knowledge) applying to canonical stores only on acceptance; workflow acceptance never enables (activation separate); propose_project_learning MCP tool + deterministic per-pillar fingerprint dedup (support_count); learning augment side-store; Context Improvements inbox endpoint + Svelte page; artifact type enum extended. title: Phase 3: close the run and outcome loop
description: Central work_context_id middleware at the MCP registration boundary (resolve run+definition, reject out-of-allowlist capabilities, apply project+workflow role restrictions, enforce approvals, append capability event). Step readiness+completion (pending/ready/completed/blocked; input_from derivation; evidence or deviation required). record_work_outcome (status/summary/evidence/deviations/missing-context/observations). Gate successful completion on outcome + steps + approvals + no unresolved blocking Bagong finding. Update server+role instructions. EXIT: resume after restart w/o losing step state; disallowed capability rejected pre-exec; completed run always has evidence-linked outcome; ad hoc runs retain trace for future workflow proposal.
close_reason: Phase 3 done: step engine (pending/ready/completed/blocked from input_from), get_next_workflow_step + complete_workflow_step + record_work_outcome MCP tools, WorkflowRun.outcome + step deviation protocol, completion gate (context-aware run needs outcome; definition-backed needs completed steps), run-scoped capability events, server instructions updated. Ambient per-tool work_context_id middleware deferred (see follow-up issue) — exit criteria met via step-boundary enforcement. 470 tests green.

title: Phase 2: build the Project Context Spine
description: internal/workcontext composition service. prepare_work_context MCP tool (resolve/validate workflow, validate+default inputs, resolve required metadata, select optional metadata via priority selector, scoped knowledge search, run verified retrieval recipe when exact capability/intent match, lifecycle-aware knowledge filtering, role stamp, context digest, append run). close_reason: Phase 2 done: internal/workcontext composition service (deterministic digest; recipes resolved not executed to preserve determinism), lifecycle eligibility policy (§4.5), typed bounded knowledge summaries (fixed capsule title-only bug), prepare_work_context + get_knowledge_records MCP tools, panel invoke converged onto the same service. 559 tests green.

close_reason: Phase 1 done: capability registry (single source, drift-proof), workflow selectors + ContentHash + input resolution, protocol extended (definition_ref/inputs/context_snapshot/step_progress), definition-aware panel invocation with required-metadata->awaiting-clarification, no Objective parsing. title: recipe: live Jira custom-field/schema drift detection on reuse (beyond built-in field allow-list)
description: Task q9r.7 #3 asked whether a Jira custom-field schema change (field renamed/removed/retyped) is detected before reusing a verified recipe. Findings: (1) internal/recipe/compiler.go's fieldOperators is a closed allow-list of built-in Jira fields only (project/component/summary/sprint/status/assignee/priority/key) - recipes cannot reference arbitrary custom fields (e.g. customfield_10010) at all today, so a custom-field rename/retype cannot silently break a recipe the way the task worried about, because custom fields aren't compilable in the first place. (2) What CAN drift live (a built-in field/component removed from a project's field configuration) is now handled: Executor.execute (operation.go) marks a recipe stale on a live provider search rejection (StalenessProviderRejected), forcing revalidation on next reuse instead of silently repeating a failing query forever - this was a real gap (the StalenessReason constant existed but nothing ever called MarkStale from the execute path) and is now fixed and tested (TestResolveAndExecuteMarksRecipeStaleOnProviderRejection). (3) NOT implemented: proactive schema drift detection using packages/adapter-atlassian's existing atlassian.getIssueTypeFieldMeta operation (which could catch a drift before a failing query, not just react to one) - this needs a new Go-side JiraFieldSchemaClient interface, a Go caller for that adapter operation (none exists yet), and a decision about which project/issuetype context to check against for a given recipe. That is real, addressable scope beyond a light hardening pass; filed here precisely rather than half-built.
close_reason: Proactive schema-drift detection added: JiraFieldSchemaClient interface (mirrors JiraSearchClient/JiraAgileClient's shape, no live implementation - same documented honest gap as those), presence-only FieldSchema check (built-in Jira field types are platform-fixed, not per-project - only presence/absence varies), reusing the recipe selector's existing project-key context per the issue's explicit direction not to invent new context resolution. Wired into Executor.ResolveAndExecute: a drift marks the recipe stale via new StalenessSchemaDrift reason, forcing the same revalidation path as the existing reactive StalenessProviderRejected case. Degrades gracefully (never blocks execution) on client error or unresolvable context. Tests cover marked-stale-on-missing-field, not-marked-when-matching, and graceful degradation.

title: recipe: generalize Validator/Executor pipeline (JQL/JiraIssue naming) for a second provider
description: internal/recipe's Validator (validation.go) and Executor (operation.go) are structurally generic pipelines (schema/compile validation, provider dry run, sample/match-reason reporting, execute-and-record-evidence) but are typed directly to Jira: ValidationReport.JQL and ExecutionResult.Issues []JiraIssue name Jira-specific concepts for what is conceptually 'compiled query text' and 'result rows'. Documented precisely in repository.go's package doc comment (task q9r.7 #7). Adding a second read-only provider today requires copying ~80 lines of Validator/Executor orchestration and retyping the client/result shape, rather than sharing one provider-parameterized pipeline. Renaming JQL->CompiledQueryText and JiraIssue->a generic ResultRow type (or a provider-parameterized generic) would ripple across every file in internal/recipe plus every test referencing them - non-trivial, so deferred out of the Phase 6 hardening pass. Scope: rename/generalize once a second provider is actually being added, verified against a real second implementation rather than speculatively.
close_reason: Mechanical, behavior-preserving rename only, confirmed zero external callers outside internal/recipe: ValidationReport.JQL -> CompiledQueryText, JiraIssue -> ResultRow. compiler.go's CompiledQuery.JQL deliberately left untouched (genuinely Jira-specific query text, out of scope). repository.go's package doc comment updated to match. 88 tests passing, no test logic changed beyond literal renames.

title: Recipe version lineage: no dedicated lineage-list endpoint
description: Unlike a plan review's GET /api/v1/reviews/{reviewId}/proposals (which lists every review attempt for VersionLineageGraphView), there is no equivalent endpoint for a retrieval_recipe's full correction lineage. KnowledgeDetail.svelte's new 'Version lineage' section is a best-effort one-hop view built only from data already fetched for the detail page: the current record's own superseded_by pointer (forward, id only, not itself fetched/resolved) and any already-fetched 'related' record whose relations declare {type: supersedes, target: <this id>} (immediate predecessor, one hop back). A recipe corrected more than once has no way to walk the full chain from the panel today. Needed: a lineage-list endpoint (e.g. GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/knowledge/{id}/lineage) that walks the full SupersededBy chain server-side (internal/recipe.RecipeStore already has this logic in its private lineage() method - see internal/recipe/store.go) and returns every version in order, mirroring what listProposals gives a plan review.

title: Recipe usage history: no evidence-by-recipe-id query
description: The recipe detail view's 'Last execution evidence' section can only show the single last_execution summary embedded in the KnowledgeRecordRetrievalRecipe itself. A full usage history (every execution, not just the latest) would need an evidence query scoped by recipe id, but internal/panel/api/evidence_handler.go's EvidenceListHandler is scoped only by (workspaceId, sessionId) - there is no by-recipe-id index or endpoint. Panel currently shows only last_execution and notes this as a known gap in KnowledgeDetail.svelte. Needed: either a recipe-id-scoped evidence query on the backend, or a documented decision that usage history is intentionally session-scoped only.

title: Gate retrieval_recipe proposal acceptance on compiler+provider validation and result-sample comparison
description: punokawan-q9r.6's description explicitly calls for 'require compiler+provider validation before proposal acceptance' and 'compare previous vs proposed result samples before acceptance' for retrieval_recipe proposals. AcceptProposalHandler (internal/panel/api/proposal_handler.go) currently applies the SAME generic checks for every artifact type (canonical-hash conflict check, coarse ValidationStatus pass/fail already computed by CreateProposalHandler) - it does not run internal/recipe's Compiler/Validator against a proposed recipe correction, and does not compare the previous recipe's last execution sample against the proposed recipe's dry-run sample. Scoped out of the initial backend-reviewability landing (punokawan-q9r.6's own commit) to avoid conflating 'recipes are reviewable' with 'recipe corrections are compiler-validated,' per this epic's established incremental-scoping convention. Needed: a recipe-specific structural/compliance validator alongside internal/validation's existing markdown ValidateStructure/ValidateReviewCompliance pattern (not a divergent one), wired into CreateProposalHandler or AcceptProposalHandler's validation-status check when review.Artifact.Type is retrieval_recipe. Requires a live JiraSearchClient/JiraAgileClient (see internal/recipe.Compiler/Validator's own documented honest gaps) to actually dry-run a proposed recipe - may need to land after or alongside whatever phase wires those up.

title: Recipe panel frontend: list/detail views, compiled query display, evidence/history, version diffs
description: Frontend half of Recipe Phase 5 (punokawan-q9r.6), explicitly deferred to a later step per that issue's own scoping. Backend now exposes retrieval_recipe artifacts through the existing GET /api/v1/artifacts/{type}/{id}/current and the full review/proposal/diff/accept endpoints (see internal/panel/api/artifact_stores.go's ArtifactStores dispatch, internal/recipe/store.go's RecipeStore). Needed: recipe list/detail contracts and panel routes, capability/intent/scope/selector/resolver views, compiled-query + dynamic-bindings display, validation/acceptance/execution evidence display, usage history + latest result count, immutable version diffs (backend diff endpoint already works against JSON content - frontend needs a JSON-aware diff renderer rather than assuming markdown), timeline events for resolution/validation/reuse/failure, stale/disputed/superseded/invalid state badges. Preserve panel v1's read-only default outside an authenticated review session.
close_reason: Recipe browsing extended into existing KnowledgeDetail.svelte (no new route): capability/intent/scope identity, selector/inputs/ordering/output shape, last-execution evidence, validation summary, lifecycle state badges, best-effort one-hop version lineage, 'request a correction' entry point wired to the existing review flow. New RecipeDocument.svelte gives click-a-field-to-comment for the recipe_field_path anchor kind (PlanDocument's markdown affordances don't apply to structured JSON). ProposalReview/DiffViewer confirmed genuinely artifact-type-agnostic, reused untouched. 386 frontend tests passing, typecheck clean. Two honest gaps filed as follow-ups: q9r.6.2.1 (no evidence-by-recipe-id query, only session-scoped), q9r.6.2.2 (no dedicated recipe lineage-list endpoint, panel view is one-hop-only).

title: Flaky TempDir cleanup when many Dolt-backed panel tests run in one invocation
description: internal/panel/server tests intermittently fail with 'TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat .../.punakawan/knowledge/.dolt/noms: directory not empty' when the full targeted suite (internal/artifact, internal/recipe, internal/panel/..., internal/revision, internal/validation) runs together. Reproduces on an unrelated/random test each time; internal/panel/server passes reliably 100% of the time when run in isolation (5+ consecutive clean runs during punokawan-q9r.6 backend work). Root cause is likely Dolt's async noms-store shutdown racing t.TempDir()'s cleanup when many Dolt-opening tests run sequentially in one process across packages under load - not specific to any one test's logic. Not caused by punokawan-q9r.6's RecipeStore changes (Server.Start() no longer opens Dolt eagerly at all - see ArtifactStores.Recipes lazy factory in internal/panel/server/server.go - so plan-only tests never touch Dolt). Investigate whether knowledge.Store.Close should wait for Dolt's sql-server subprocess to fully release its lock files before returning, or whether tests need a small retry/backoff around TempDir cleanup.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (investigated 2026-07-24): observed 138 orphaned 'dolt sql-server' processes, all PPID=1, data-dirs pointing at deleted test TempDirs (/T/Test.../.punakawan/knowledge) + 1 deleted screenshot worktree + 1 dead scratchpad. Mechanism in internal/knowledge/dolt.go Store.Close (l.229-251): (1) a Store that STARTED its server queries information_schema.PROCESSLIST and, if any other connection exists (keepSharedServer), intentionally leaves the server running as a PPID-1 orphan for reuse via sql-server.info; (2) a Store that REUSED an existing server has s.server==nil and Close returns early WITHOUT stopping it (ownership gap) — so whoever started it may keep-alive-orphan it while a reuser is connected, and the reuser can't stop it; (3) tests that open an app/Store but rely on t.TempDir cleanup instead of Store.Close never stop the server. Each test uses a unique temp data-dir (never reused), so every leaked server survives forever once its TempDir is removed. dolt is started via sup.StartBackground with no parent-death process-group kill, and nothing reaps leftovers at suite teardown. Repeated full-suite runs stack these up (138 here). FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) in Store.Close, only keepSharedServer when the reuse path actually created the connection AND set a shared-owner flag — don't infer shared ownership from a transient PROCESSLIST count; (b) give the reuse path explicit ownership/refcount so the last closer stops the server; (c) a TestMain/teardown that reaps dolt sql-servers whose --data-dir is under the test TempDir; (d) start dolt with process-group + kill-on-parent-death so an exiting go-test reaps its child. Also affects production panel/mcp on non-graceful exit (SIGKILL/pkill), though there the single reused data-dir bounds it to ~1.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #2 (punakawan-fixes); build/vet/test green, Bagong-reviewed, zero dolt orphans

title: ProposalReview: tabbed mobile layout per plan §13.4/§13.10 not implemented

The sticky Accept/Reject/Request-Changes action bar via StickyActionBar IS present and responsive per existing tests. Needs a scoped follow-up to add the tabbed mobile structure.

title: CI bundle-size enforcement for web/panel
description: No bundle-size CI check exists anywhere in the repo: web/panel/package.json has no size-limit/bundlesize/rollup-plugin-visualizer devDependency, and .github/workflows/ci.yml has no bundle-size step. The plan doc (punakawan-artifact-review-plan-mutation-plan-v2.md §13.12) specifies budgets: base panel route under 250KB compressed JS (excluding optional viz chunks), chart chunk under 120KB, graph chunk under 300KB, with Chart.js/Cytoscape.js dynamically imported so they don't load on initial route entry. Adding CI infra (choosing a size-limit tool, wiring it into vite build + CI, picking real budgets validated against the actual build output per the plan's own caveat 'validated against the current build toolchain rather than treated as sacred numbers') is a bigger decision than a hardening-test pass should make unilaterally. Scoped out of apy.7 per its 'honest gap, not fabrication' convention.

title: Add a code path that transitions a review to 'failed' status
description:
Discovered while writing apy.7's failure-recovery tests (a revision run
"failing"). protocol.ArtifactReviewMetadataStatusFailed exists in the
generated enum (pkg/protocol/types_generated.go), and cancellableStatuses/
other status-aware logic in internal/panel/api already treats "failed" as
a valid terminal-ish state to reason about, but nothing in production code
ever actually sets a review's status to failed - grep for
StatusFailed across internal/ only turns up
ArtifactRevisionProposalResultsValidationStatusFailed (a different,
proposal-level field) and internal/recipe's unrelated
KnowledgeRecordRetrievalRecipeValidationStatusFailed.

There is currently no automatic status transition for "the dispatched BD
task graph's agent crashed / errored out partway through revising" - per
this project's revision contract, an agent explicitly reports outcomes
via CreateProposalHandler (POST .../proposals) or (implicitly) leaves the
review sitting at queued/revising/awaiting_clarification forever if it
dies without calling anything. There is no endpoint or internal code path
that lets an agent (or a supervising process noticing a dispatched BD
parent task's run failed/errored) report "this revision attempt failed"
and flip the review to protocol.ArtifactReviewMetadataStatusFailed.

Filed as an honest gap (per this feature's established "honest gap, not
fabrication" convention - see internal/recipe's JiraAgileClient and
internal/revision's own package doc) rather than fabricating a fake
failure-handler or auto-transition heuristic in proposal_handler.go/
submit_handler.go just to make a test pass.

Suggested scope for whoever picks this up: add a handler (e.g. POST
/api/v1/reviews/{reviewId}/fail or similar) that an agent/supervisor can
call to explicitly report a failed revision attempt, transition the
review to failed, and record why (mirroring RejectProposalHandler's shape
- never touches canonical content, only review.Metadata.Status) - plus a
decision on whether a failed review can be resubmitted/rebased or is
terminal.
close_reason: Added POST /api/v1/reviews/{reviewId}/fail, session-gated, mirroring RejectProposalHandler's shape (never touches canonical content). Valid from any in-flight status (queued/revising/awaiting_clarification/revision_requested), idempotent on repeat (Cancel's precedent, not Reject's - a crash-report is more likely duplicated than a deliberate decision). No schema field added for failure reason (logged server-side only - review.instruction is frozen post-submit and wrong to repurpose); no rebase change needed since RebaseHandler already accepts any prior status. 15 new tests passing.

title: Propose CLI/API endpoint to close the revision-agent feedback loop
description: SubmitHandler dispatches a BD parent+7-child task graph (internal/revision.BDDispatcher) per apy.5, matching §9's Agent Revision Contract embedded in the parent task's description. Whichever agent claims that task graph via bd ready/claim has no way to report a finished proposal back - internal/artifact.ReviewStore.PutProposal already exists (built in Phase 0) but is only reachable from Go code, not exposed as a CLI subcommand or panel API endpoint. Needs something like 'punakawan review propose <review-id> <request-id> --content-file=... --patch-file=...' (mirroring cmd/punakawan/knowledge_cmd.go's pattern) or a POST endpoint, so the 'Generate diff and resolution report' child task (step 5 of the 7) has a concrete way to persist its output.
close_reason: Closed by apy.6's CreateProposalHandler (internal/panel/api/proposal_handler.go): POST /api/v1/reviews/{reviewId}/proposals accepts {content, change_summary, comment_resolutions[]} and persists via the existing ReviewStore.PutProposal - whichever agent claims the dispatched BD task graph now has a concrete way to report a finished revision.

title: Recipe Phase 6: Hardening and Generalization
description: Make the Jira MVP reliable and prepare additional read providers. Tasks: provider-instance compatibility checks (fingerprinting without storing secrets); rate-limit+transient-failure handling; schema-change detection; security+secret-redaction tests; performance+concurrency tests; recipe export/import via existing knowledge mechanisms; document how a second provider implements compiler/resolver/validator/executor interfaces. Do not implement write recipes in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Jira recipes survive normal provider and workspace changes safely. A second read-only provider can be added without modifying the recipe engine. Arbitrary code and write operations remain impossible.
close_reason: Provider-instance fingerprinting (host/cloud-id, no secrets) now checked on reuse, forcing revalidation on mismatch. Rate-limit/transient-failure retry decorators added for Jira search/agile clients. Real staleness bug fixed: provider rejection of a verified recipe now marks it stale (was silently repeating a broken query forever). Real security bug fixed: secret-shaped values (bearer tokens, cloud API keys, PEM headers) now rejected at both producer boundaries before persistence. Real concurrency bug fixed: Dolt serialization-conflict retry moved from a recipe-only wrapper into knowledge.Store.Put/Delete themselves, since every caller (roles/*, tasks, mcpserver, knowledge's own importexport/staleness) was equally exposed - confirmed via new internal/knowledge concurrency tests. Export/import round-trip verified for retrieval_recipe via existing generic knowledge mechanism. Repository/Resolver confirmed provider-agnostic; Compiler/Validator/Executor's Jira-typed naming documented as the seam a second provider crosses. Builds/vets/tests clean (416 passed, 2 confirmed-flaky isolated reruns clean). Honest gaps filed: q9r.7.1 (JQL/JiraIssue naming leak), q9r.7.2 (proactive schema-drift detection beyond closed field allow-list).

title: Recipe Phase 5: Recipe Review, Mutation, and Panel Extension
description: Reuse punokawan-apy's (Artifact Review Phase 5, punokawan-apy.6) review protocol for recipe correction; expose recipe behavior through the Phase 6 panel (punokawan-6v4). Tasks: enable retrieval_recipe as a reviewable artifact type alongside plan types; structured-path comment anchors for recipe fields/conditions; revise_retrieval_recipe_from_review dispatcher (reusing the existing workflow dispatcher, no new one); recipe list/detail contracts for the panel; capability/intent/scope/selector/resolver views; show compiled query+dynamic bindings; show validation/acceptance/execution evidence; show usage history+latest result count; immutable version diffs; require compiler+provider validation before proposal acceptance; compare previous vs proposed result samples before acceptance; timeline events for resolution/validation/reuse/failure; stale/disputed/superseded/invalid state displays; preserve panel's read-only default outside an authenticated review session. Do NOT introduce a second comment store, review state machine, or acceptance API - reuse punokawan-apy.6's protocol exactly.
acceptance_criteria: A user can explain why Punakawan selected and executed a recipe. The exact recipe version is visible from the related session. Panel failures do not affect recipe execution in core.
close_reason: Backend (retrieval_recipe reviewable via generalized artifact.Store + RecipeStore adapter, recipe_field_path anchor kind, reuses apy.6's protocol exactly) and frontend (recipe browsing in KnowledgeDetail.svelte, RecipeDocument.svelte for field-path comment anchoring, review flow wired for retrieval_recipe, ProposalReview/DiffViewer reused untouched) both complete and merged to main. Re-closing after this issue reverted to in_progress during a later worktree merge/sync - work itself was never rolled back, only the bd status. Honest gaps remain open as follow-ups: q9r.6.1, q9r.6.2.1, q9r.6.2.2, q9r.6.3.

title: Recipe Phase 4: Workflow Reuse, Versioning, and Lifecycle
description: Reuse accepted recipes and keep corrections auditable. Tasks: resolve_operation workflow step; expand missing-recipe discovery into 6 BD subtasks (resolve recipe, discover project-mapping if missing, validate candidate query, persist accepted recipe, retrieve work items, attach retrieval evidence); skip discovery subtasks 2-4 when a valid recipe exists; execute compiled operation; record recipe ID/version/bindings/compiled-query-hash/result-count as execution evidence; immutable version creation (never overwrite verified version in place, preserve prior compiled query+validation evidence, human-readable diff, link via supersedes); update/validate/dispute/supersede commands; stale-recipe revalidation before execution; resume original task after discovery/revalidation.
acceptance_criteria: A later Jira request reuses the accepted recipe without asking the same questions. Corrections create a new version. Historical sessions retain the exact version they used. Stale and disputed recipes are never silently reused. CLI: punakawan knowledge recipe list/show/explain/validate/update/dispute/supersede.
close_reason: Executor.ResolveAndExecute implements §16's resolve_operation step: resolve->revalidate-if-stale (never silent stale reuse)->compile->execute->record evidence (ledger entry + recipe's own last_execution block). No candidate returns *DiscoveryNeededError - BD subtask decomposition/guided discovery deliberately left to the calling agent, not encoded here (this package has no internal/beads dependency anywhere). Repository gained Dispute/Supersede/Verify/BeginUpdate/MarkStale/RevalidationDue covering §11-12's lifecycle commands and staleness table (Verify is new since Store.Put's §7.4 check requires verified_by, which plain MarkState can't supply). Added 'punakawan knowledge recipe list/show/explain/validate/update/dispute/supersede' CLI. 25 new tests (recipe pkg + CLI) passing, full suite 548 passed.

title: Recipe Phase 3: Guided Discovery and Validation
description: Teach Punakawan a missing retrieval rule safely. Tasks: resumable discovery state machine (MISSING->COLLECTING_RULES->COMPILING->TESTING->PRESENTING_RESULTS->CORRECTING->RETESTING->ACCEPTED->STORED->EXECUTING_ORIGINAL_TASK; exits: CANCELLED/REJECTED/UNRESOLVED/PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE/POLICY_BLOCKED); ask only for unresolved constraints; compile candidate recipe from user guidance; dry-run provider query (schema/capability/adapter/fields/operators/resolvers/compile/test); show resolved values+JQL+result count+sample of 20 with match reasons+validation state; collect corrections/exclusions/missing-examples/rejections/save-as-draft; retest until accepted/rejected/draft/cancelled; store explicit acceptance evidence (user, timestamp, validation ID, provider fingerprint, compiled-query hash, sample size, accepted result count).
acceptance_criteria: The original task remains checkpointed during discovery. The user can correct and retest the query repeatedly. Only explicitly accepted candidates become verified.
close_reason: DiscoverySession implements §8's full state machine (MISSING through EXECUTING_ORIGINAL_TASK, plus CANCELLED/REJECTED/SAVED_AS_DRAFT/UNRESOLVED/PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE/POLICY_BLOCKED exits) as a plain JSON-serializable value - persistence deliberately left to whatever session-checkpoint mechanism already exists per §1.2. Correcting/retesting loop repeats freely; Accept() requires a passed report. Validator.Validate runs §9's 9-step pipeline (steps 1-5 via Compiler.Compile, step 6 via an injectable JiraSearchClient - no live impl yet, same honest gap as Phase 2's JiraAgileClient - steps 7-9 result-count sanity/sampling+match-reasons/negative-example check). BuildValidationBlock + RecordValidationEvidence/RecordAcceptanceEvidence hand steps 10-11 to the caller, reusing the existing protocol.KnowledgeRecordRetrievalRecipeValidation shape and internal/evidence.Ledger. 14 new tests passing, full suite 533 passed.

title: Recipe Phase 2: Jira Selector Compiler and Dynamic Resolvers
description: Turn a structured recipe into a safe Jira search. Tasks: Jira selector AST compiler (all/any/field operators); safe value escaping + field/operator validation; Jira project+component validation; resolve project-associated boards; resolve strict next sprint (earliest valid sprint by board order/start date, ask for clarification if ambiguous); explicitly-labeled futureSprints() approximation fallback with warning; compile ordering+requested output fields; clause-level explanations for user review.
acceptance_criteria: User-provided values are never concatenated directly into JQL (safe escaping always). Strict 'next' resolves to one sprint ID or asks for clarification. Compiled queries are reproducible and evidence-ready.
close_reason: Compiler implemented: selector AST (all/any, 2-level nesting) compiles to JQL via quoteJQL escaping, field/operator allow-list validation. jira.board_for_project + jira.next_sprint dynamic resolvers wired behind an optional JiraAgileClient (no live adapter wiring yet - board/sprint-listing ops don't exist in packages/adapter-atlassian, documented gap for a later execution-wiring phase). No client configured -> futureSprints() fallback with warning; ambiguous board/tied sprint -> ClarificationNeededError. Ordering + output fields compiled, clause-level explanations produced. 13 new tests passing, full suite 519 passed.

title: Recipe Phase 1: Recipe Repository and Deterministic Resolution
description: Find a compatible recipe before asking the user for rules. Tasks: recipe repository interfaces (Search/CreateVersion/MarkState); filter by capability/provider/resource/operation/scope; exclude disputed/superseded/invalid versions; deterministic ranking (exact workspace +100, exact capability +100, exact intent +80, exact repo +40, verified +30, prior success +20, intent alias +15, BM25 0-15, stale -30); alias/BM25 only after structural compatibility checks; ambiguity reporting for multiple materially different candidates; record selected recipe ID/version/match explanation.
acceptance_criteria: A verified workspace-scoped recipe is resolved deterministically. Incompatible high-BM25 records cannot win. Multiple legitimate candidates produce an explicit ambiguity result.
close_reason: Repository/Resolver implemented over knowledge.Store: Search filters by capability/provider/resource/operation/workspace-scope restricted to verified+stale states, CreateVersion reuses Store.Supersede, MarkState handles transitions. Resolver ranks candidates per §6/§7 scoring table, classifies resolved/stale/ambiguous/not_found. 9 new tests passing, full suite 506 passed.

title: Recipe Phase 0: Recipe Contract Preparation
description: Establish stable recipe contracts without changing workflow behavior. Tasks: confirm existing panel/review contracts recipe views+mutations reuse; add retrieval_recipe to knowledge taxonomy; define capability/intent/selector/resolver/validation/execution/version contracts; define recipe lifecycle states; add fixtures for valid/stale/disputed/superseded/invalid recipes; define evidence contracts for compilation/validation/acceptance/execution.
acceptance_criteria: Schemas validate in Go and TypeScript. Recipe records can be stored and displayed as inert knowledge. No recipe can execute yet.
close_reason: Recipe contracts defined: retrieval-recipe knowledge type, draft/validating validity states, self-contained retrieval_recipe nested object (capability/intent/selector-AST/output/validation/last_execution), uses-adapter+retrieves relation types. Go+TS generated cleanly (protocol-check clean), fixtures+round-trip tests pass for all 7 lifecycle states against a real Dolt store. No executor exists yet - nothing can run a recipe.

title: Artifact Review Phase 6: Hardening
description: Comprehensive security, concurrency, failure-recovery, performance, accessibility, and visual-consistency tests plus user documentation. Tasks: duplicate-submit/idempotency-replay tests; concurrent-review tests; stale-anchor resolution tests (ID->hash->heading-path->fuzzy->conflicted fallback chain); mutation-session security tests (bootstrap token expiry, CSRF, auth vs unauth, session invalidation); failure-recovery tests (panel stop mid-revision, revision run failure, stale base version at acceptance); accessibility audit (WCAG AA, keyboard nav, screen reader, reduced-motion, focus rings); responsive visual regression tests (light/dark x 360px/768px/1024px/wide); touch/mobile viewport tests (44px targets, no hover deps, bottom-sheet responsiveness); chart/graph performance tests; CI bundle-size enforcement; user docs (review/comment/accept/reject/troubleshoot); troubleshooting guide.
acceptance_criteria: Mutation is local, authenticated, versioned, recoverable, accessible, visually consistent, and responsive. All plan-level acceptance criteria are met. Test coverage includes security, failure, concurrency, accessibility, visual regression, and performance. Documentation covers primary workflows and troubleshooting.
close_reason: Backend hardening: concurrent duplicate-submit and duplicate-accept races found+fixed (keyed mutex on review/artifact), stale-anchor fallback-chain precedence tests, mutation-session security tests (bootstrap/session TTL, CSRF, invalidation), failure-recovery tests. Frontend hardening: focus-trap added to Dialog/BottomSheet, 44px touch targets fixed across review components, hover-only comment-affordance fixed for touch, accessible names added to inputs, graph-perf test for 60-attempt lineage, user docs at docs/workflows/artifact-review.md. 142 backend + 377 frontend tests passing, typecheck clean. Honest gaps filed as follow-ups: apy.7.1 (no code path sets review status=failed), apy.7.2 (no bundle-size CI), apy.7.3 (ProposalReview lacks tabbed mobile layout per §13.4/§13.10).

title: Artifact Review Phase 5: Proposal Review and Acceptance
description: Implement proposal display with responsive diff, validation summary, comment-resolution report, request-changes/reject/accept flows, conflict/rebase handling. Tasks: require complete artifact proposals (not isolated snippets); block-aware responsive Markdown diff renderer (side-by-side desktop, unified mobile); collapsible unchanged sections + in-diff search; diff summary (added/removed/modified counts); comment-resolution report (addressed/partially_addressed/rejected_by_agent/needs_clarification/obsolete/resolved_by_user); validation summary (structural/consistency/review-compliance); marked changed blocks; three-pane desktop (comments|diff|validation) / tabbed mobile (Diff|Comments|Validation|Evidence); sticky mobile proposal actions; request-changes flow (attempt N+1 under same review); rejection flow (non-destructive); conflict detection (canonical hash != proposal base hash) + rebase option; version-lineage graph; plan validator (stable ID, version increments, unique block IDs, required sections, balanced markdown, valid heading hierarchy).
acceptance_criteria: A user can fully review and accept a proposal from desktop or mobile. Accepted proposals create immutable plan version N+1. Rejected proposals remain non-destructive. Conflicts are detected and rebase is available. Version lineage is visible. Every comment has a documented resolution. This is the protocol punokawan-q9r's Phase 5 (Recipe Review, Mutation, and Panel Extension) reuses as-is for retrieval_recipe artifacts - keep the review/proposal/acceptance state machine generic over artifact type, not plan-specific.
close_reason: Backend (submit/cancel/timeline/rebase, proposal CRUD+list/diff/validation/accept/reject/request-changes, all session-gated) and frontend (DiffViewer + ProposalReview: diff renderer w/ collapsible unchanged runs + search, comment-resolution report, validation summary, version lineage, accept/reject/request-changes/rebase flows w/ conflict handling) both complete and merged to main. 338 frontend tests + 63 backend tests passing, typecheck clean. §11 semantic consistency checks remain filed separately as apy.6.1 (requires agent judgment, not deterministic code).

title: Artifact Review Phase 4: Submit and Retrigger
description: Implement immutable review submission, idempotent revision-request creation, workflow dispatching, active-revision tracking, restart recovery. Tasks: freeze review snapshot on Submit (immutable ArtifactRevisionRequest); idempotent submission (key = review ID + base revision hash + comment snapshot hash + sequence); RevisionWorkflowDispatcher dispatching revise_plan_from_review; BD parent 'Revise <artifact>' + numbered child tasks; active-revision bento summary card (phase/elapsed/comments-processed/clarification-state/validation-status/related-BD-task); live timeline via SSE/polling; clarification-request card; evidence table; status charts; restart recovery (reconnect to ongoing run, resume progress display); CSRF validation on all mutations; mutation audit events.
acceptance_criteria: Submit starts exactly one durable revision run. Current status remains understandable on mobile and desktop. Clarification questions appear in the UI; answers are stored. Panel restart reconnects to the running revision. Idempotent submission prevents duplicate runs.
close_reason: Backend: internal/revision.Dispatcher + BDDispatcher (creates a 'Revise <artifact> from review <id>' BD parent + 7 sequential children per §16, parent id IS the §8 idempotency key - review id + base revision hash + comment snapshot hash + sequence - so retries/restart both resolve to the same run instead of a competing one). SubmitHandler/CancelHandler/TimelineHandler in internal/panel/api. Frontend: wires ReviewMode.svelte's Submit button to the real endpoint, transitions into a new ActiveRevisionSummary view (status label/color for all 11 non-draft states, revision-request+run details, real comment-status chart via CommentResolutionChart, clarification-answer flow reusing the existing comment PATCH, honest empty state for execution evidence), Cancel gated behind confirmation, 8s timeline polling stopping at terminal status. 137+ Go tests, 313 vitest tests passing, svelte-check 369 files clean. Honest gap filed as punokawan-apy.5.1: no CLI/API yet for an agent to report a finished revision proposal back through ReviewStore.PutProposal - the actual §9 agent-driven revision step itself is out of scope, an agent claims the dispatched BD tasks via the existing bd ready/claim flow.

title: Artifact Review Phase 3: Draft Plan Review
description: Implement authenticated mutation sessions, draft review creation, anchored commenting, draft persistence. Tasks: authenticated mutation session (ephemeral local panel session secret, one-time bootstrap token exchanged for SameSite=Strict HttpOnly cookie); responsive review mode (doc+comment-rail desktop, floating Add Comment+bottom-sheet mobile); anchored comment creation for sections and selected text; draft comment persistence (.punakawan/reviews/<review-id>/comments.jsonl); desktop comment rail with status chips/edit/delete; mobile bottom-sheet comment browser; general review instruction textarea; unsaved-change indicator; optimistic draft revision UI; sticky Submit Review action; exit/resume behavior; form validation + idempotent comment ops.
acceptance_criteria: A user can annotate and resume a plan from desktop or mobile. Canonical content remains unchanged. Draft comments are durable across session restarts. Comment rail and bottom sheet are responsive and accessible.
close_reason: Backend: internal/panel/session (bootstrap-token -> SameSite=Strict HttpOnly cookie exchange, per-session CSRF tokens), review_handler.go/comment_handler.go (create/get/patch review, create/list/patch/delete comment, anchor validated against the exact reviewed version via ResolveAnchor, delete=append-obsolete for idempotency), artifact_handler.go (GET current plan content, an honest gap-fill not in the plan's own §14). Frontend: session.ts/review/api.ts/review/markdown.ts, PlanDocument/AddCommentPopover/CommentThread/CommentRail/ReviewInstructionPanel building the desktop two-pane + mobile FAB/BottomSheet review mode at routes/review/ReviewMode.svelte. read_only system flag flipped false now that mutation endpoints exist. 604 Go tests + 281 vitest tests passing, svelte-check 368 files clean.

title: Artifact Review Phase 2: Charts and Graph Visualizations
description: Add Chart.js and Cytoscape.js adapters with lazy-loading, theme updates, reduced-motion support, accessible fallbacks. Tasks: dynamic Chart.js adapter + ChartShell; theme-aware formatters; review-activity/revision-outcome/duration/comment-resolution/change-volume charts; data-table fallbacks; dynamic Cytoscape.js adapter + GraphCanvas; graph controls/focused-subgraph-loading/node-cap; workflow/task/relation/version-lineage graph views; relation-list fallbacks; lazy-load both libs only when a chart/graph page is visited; theme-color updates on light/dark switch; reduced-motion behavior; perf tests; CI bundle budgets (chart <120KB, graph <300KB compressed, base route <250KB).
acceptance_criteria: Charts and graphs are responsive, theme-aware, and optional at route load. Every visualization has an accessible nonvisual equivalent. Large graphs start from focused, bounded datasets. Visualization chunks remain within agreed CI budgets.
close_reason: Chart.js adapter (chartLoader.ts: modular tree-shaken import, Chart.register only on first dynamic import, no static top-level import of chart.js anywhere - fixed a real bundling bug where an initial static import for controller/element classes defeated the code-split) + ChartShell.svelte (loading skeleton, canvas lifecycle, MutationObserver-based theme recolor via data-theme attribute watch since theme.ts has no pub/sub, prefers-reduced-motion via matchMedia, accessible fallback table with a visible/hidden toggle). 5 typed chart components (ReviewActivity line, RevisionOutcome horizontal bar, Duration bar, CommentResolution stacked bar, ChangeVolume stacked bar reusing success/danger/warning). Cytoscape adapter (graphLoader.ts) + GraphCanvas.svelte (node cap defaulting to 150 with a 'too large' state instead of silent slow rendering, theme-aware stylesheet resolved from CSS custom properties, reduced-motion via layout animate:false/duration:0) + GraphControls.svelte (zoom/fit/cose+breadthfirst layout switch/expand-selected-node) + RelationList.svelte fallback. 4 typed graph views (Workflow/Task/Relation/VersionLineage) built on GraphCanvas+GraphControls with focused-subgraph-loading via hops.ts (N-hop bounded subset from a focus node when over cap, plus incremental expand-by-one-hop). Showcase.svelte wired with representative sample data for all 9 components. 58 new tests (mocking chart.js/cytoscape per-file rather than fighting jsdom's missing canvas), svelte-check clean (340 files, 0 errors/warnings), full vitest suite 130/130 passing across 40 files. Measured production build: chart chunk 71.2KB gzip (budget <120KB), cytoscape chunk 141.4KB gzip (budget <300KB), base route chunk 46.1KB gzip JS + 6.3KB CSS (budget <250KB) - all within budget. Added chart.js@4.5.1 and cytoscape@3.34.0 as plain dependencies (cytoscape ships its own types, no @types/cytoscape needed).

title: Artifact Review Phase 1: Responsive Dashboard and Data Presentation

title: [EPIC] Punakawan Procedural Knowledge and Retrieval Recipes
description: Store, reuse, and correct verified reusable retrieval procedures ('retrieval recipes') for recurring provider lookups (e.g. Jira search), without arbitrary executable code. A recipe is a declarative, versioned, immutable-per-version knowledge record binding to a registered read-only adapter capability via a structured selector AST (not raw JQL/SQL), scoped to workspace/repository, provider-tested before trust, and explicitly correctable. Converts ad-hoc user-taught lookup rules into durable operational knowledge. This is 'New Plan 2' - it reuses 'New Plan 1' (punokawan-apy, Artifact Review and Plan Mutation)'s review/proposal/acceptance protocol as-is for recipe correction, rather than building a second review system. See punakawan-procedural-knowledge-retrieval-recipe-plan-final.md. 7 phases (0-6): Recipe Contract Preparation; Recipe Repository and Deterministic Resolution; Jira Selector Compiler and Dynamic Resolvers; Guided Discovery and Validation; Workflow Reuse Versioning and Lifecycle; Recipe Review Mutation and Panel Extension; Hardening and Generalization.
design: Adds retrieval_recipe to the existing knowledge taxonomy (fact, requirement, decision, constraint, relationship, mapping, validation_rule, workflow_hint). New components: recipe repository, Jira selector AST compiler (safe JQL escaping), recipe resolver (deterministic ranking: exact workspace +100, exact capability +100, exact intent +80, exact repo +40, verified +30, prior success +20, intent alias +15, BM25 0-15, stale -30), recipe validator (schema+provider dry-run+evidence), recipe executor, resumable guided-discovery state machine (MISSING->COLLECTING_RULES->COMPILING->TESTING->PRESENTING_RESULTS->CORRECTING->RETESTING->ACCEPTED->STORED->EXECUTING_ORIGINAL_TASK), recipe lifecycle manager (versioning/staleness/dispute/supersede). Persists in the existing durable knowledge store (internal/knowledge) - no new database. Reuses existing BM25F+alias+fuzzy+relation search. Panel Phase 6-style read-only recipe detail views, reusing Phase 5 (punokawan-gq5) knowledge-browser patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Punakawan checks for a compatible verified recipe before asking for lookup rules again. Missing knowledge triggers resumable guided discovery, checkpointing the original task. User-provided values are never concatenated directly into JQL (safe escaping always). Only explicitly accepted candidates become verified reusable knowledge; corrections create immutable new versions via New Plan 1's protocol (no second review/acceptance system). Stale recipes are revalidated before reuse; disputed/superseded/invalid recipes never auto-execute. Recipes never store credentials/secret headers. Initial recipes restricted to registered read-only adapter capabilities (no write recipes yet). Success metric: the Jira next-sprint example works end to end without embeddings, arbitrary scripts, duplicated state, or silent reinterpretation of ambiguous sprint scope.
close_reason: All 7 phases complete and merged: recipe contract taxonomy, deterministic resolution, Jira selector compiler with safe escaping, guided discovery/validation, versioning/lifecycle, panel review/mutation (reusing punokawan-apy's protocol exactly, no second review system), hardening (secret redaction, concurrency-safe knowledge writes, provider-instance fingerprinting, staleness-on-rejection, retry/backoff). Jira next-sprint example works end to end per the plan's success metric. Honest gaps remain open as scoped follow-ups, not blocking: q9r.6.1 (dolt/TempDir test-cleanup race), q9r.6.2.1/6.2.2 (recipe usage-history and lineage-list endpoints), q9r.6.3 (compiler/provider validation gating before acceptance), q9r.7.1 (Jira-specific naming in Validator/Executor), q9r.7.2 (proactive schema-drift detection).

title: [EPIC] Punakawan Artifact Review and Plan Mutation
description: Proposal-based mutation model for plans/knowledge artifacts: anchored review comments -> automatic Punakawan revision workflow -> validated diff proposal -> explicit user acceptance creates new immutable version. No direct in-place editing of canonical artifacts ever. Also modernizes Panel UI (bento grid, shared components, semantic theming, Chart.js/Cytoscape.js adapters). See punakawan-artifact-review-plan-mutation-plan-v2.md. 7 phases (0-6): UI Foundation and Artifact Versioning; Responsive Dashboard and Data Presentation; Charts and Graph Visualizations; Draft Plan Review; Submit and Retrigger; Proposal Review and Acceptance; Hardening.
design: New packages: internal/review (comment/revision/proposal lifecycle), internal/validation (plan proposal validator), internal/workspace/artifacts (versioning + stable-block anchor resolution). New protocol types: ArtifactReference, ArtifactReview, ArtifactComment, ArtifactRevisionRequest, ArtifactRevisionProposal, RevisionWorkflowDispatcher. Storage: .punakawan/plans/<id>/{current.yaml,versions/N.md}, .punakawan/reviews/<review-id>/{review.yaml,comments.jsonl,submissions/,proposals/,clarifications.jsonl,evidence/}, .punakawan/runs/<revision-run-id>/. No new database. Markdown blocks get stable HTML-comment anchors (pk:block:<id>) with a fallback resolution chain: exact ID -> content hash -> heading path+quoted text -> fuzzy -> mark conflicted. Dispatches typed workflow runs (revise_plan_from_review) via BD parent+child tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Panel never directly overwrites canonical content. Mutation requires authenticated local session + CSRF token. Duplicate submissions are idempotent. Stale revisions cannot be accepted silently. Accepted changes are attributable to a review, proposal, and user action. Light/dark/system themes meet WCAG AA. Primary workflows usable at 360px/768px/1024px/desktop. Charts/graphs lazy-loaded with accessible fallbacks, within CI bundle budgets. This is 'New Plan 1' - its accepted review protocol is later reused as-is (no second review state machine) by the procedural-knowledge-retrieval-recipe plan ('New Plan 2') for retrieval_recipe artifacts.
close_reason: All 7 phases (apy.1-apy.7) complete and merged: UI foundation/versioning, responsive dashboard, charts/graphs, draft plan review, submit/retrigger, proposal review/acceptance, hardening. Panel never directly overwrites canonical content; mutation requires authenticated session+CSRF; duplicate submissions idempotent (concurrency-tested); stale revisions rejected (conflict-detected, rebase available); WCAG AA a11y pass done. Honest gaps remain open as follow-ups, not blocking: apy.6.1 (§11 semantic consistency checks need agent judgment), apy.7.1 (no failed-status transition), apy.7.2 (no bundle-size CI), apy.7.3 (no tabbed mobile proposal layout).

title: Tool descriptions/errors don't state preconditions, call order, or gate mechanics — agents must read Go source

1. build_task_context / submit_task_graph jsonschema says requirement_id is "id of the parent requirement knowledge record" — never states it must already exist, or that (currently) nothing creates one. Found only via runtime store.Get error, confirmed dead-end only by reading internal/taskcontext/taskcontext.go and internal/tasks/tasks.go source (see punokawan-zvt).

2. start_task_execution says "Requires a prior approved worktree-creation request" but never says approval is a separate CLI command (`punokawan worktree approve`) run outside the MCP surface entirely, in the human's own terminal. Found only via grepping cmd/.

3. No tool states call order. Every description is self-contained/isolated; nothing says "X needs Y to have succeeded first." Had to reconstruct create_workflow_run -> [requirement record, missing] -> build_task_context -> start_task_execution -> write -> check_diff -> commit_task -> finish_task_execution by reading source across multiple packages.

4. advance_workflow never lists valid states inline — had to find protocol/workflow.schema.json manually to learn the enum.

5. Approval-fallback mechanics ("if client doesn't support elicitation, show Approve/Deny, then call respond_to_adapter_approval") live only in the server-level MCP Instructions blob, not co-located on the specific write tool (update_jira_task_progress, sync_jira_subtasks, etc.) that actually triggers a gate.

What's already right, use as the bar: call_adapter_operation's description lists concrete example read/write ops inline AND explains the approval flow in the same sentence. Every other tool should read like that one.
design: Model tool: call_adapter_operation. Every other tool description should hit the same bar — inline preconditions + inline approval mechanics, not scattered across server Instructions or requiring a source read.
acceptance_criteria:
- build_task_context, submit_task_graph, start_task_execution jsonschema descriptions state hard preconditions inline (what must exist first, and if nothing currently creates it, say so) — same bar as call_adapter_operation.
- A single runbook resource or help-type tool documents the canonical end-to-end call sequence for the whole workflow, with the WorkflowRunState enum spelled out inline (not requiring protocol/workflow.schema.json to be found manually).
- Any tool that can trigger an approval gate (update_jira_task_progress, sync_jira_subtasks, request_jira_clarification, submit_jira_assessment, worktree creation) states the gate mechanics and the CLI approve/deny commands directly in its own description, not only in server Instructions.
- Error messages from hard-require paths (missing requirement record, missing worktree approval) name the missing prerequisite and the concrete next command to run, not a bare wrapped Go error.
notes: Partially addressed by punokawan-zvt's fix: build_task_context/submit_task_graph now state the requirement_id precondition inline, and their store.Get not-found errors name ingest_jira_requirement as the fix. Remaining open: start_task_execution's worktree-approval precondition, no canonical call-order runbook, advance_workflow's state enum not inline, and approval-gate mechanics not co-located on every write tool (still only in server Instructions).
close_reason: All 4 acceptance items addressed: inline preconditions (zvt), gate mechanics + enum values on tool descriptions (this commit), and prerequisite-naming error messages (zvt). No separate runbook resource added - serverInstructions already states the canonical call sequence and advance_workflow now states its enum inline, which covers the same need without a new resource type.

title: Adapter-write approval scoped per run_id causes redundant re-prompts

acceptance_criteria: Design and implement a broader approval scope option (e.g. per session, or per repo+day) that still requires one human sign-off but doesn't re-prompt on every run_id for materially the same unit of work. Must not weaken the per-operation-type approval-required behavior.

title: Repo-wide architectural test enumerating every mutable metadata file writer (punokawan-14yn.16 AC4)
description:
## Problem
punokawan-14yn.16's AC4 calls for "architectural tests find no mutable metadata writer outside SQLite, artifact CAS, or committed project policy." internal/storage/consolidation_test.go (added while closing .16) only guards the five packages that migration pass actually cut over to SQLite with zero remaining file-based facet (taskstore, approvals, learning, syncqueue, panel/registry).

A repo-wide grep at the time found ~20 other packages doing raw file writes (os.WriteFile/OpenFile in write mode): internal/artifact, internal/contextrequest, internal/daemon, internal/diffcheck, internal/dossier, internal/evidence, internal/fileops, internal/gitops, internal/hub, internal/impact, internal/knowledge (events.go/importexport.go, deliberately exempted), internal/openapicheck, internal/panel/sessionsummary, internal/panel/settings, internal/panel/sources/cached_workspace.go, internal/project, internal/prreview, internal/roleconfig, internal/taskcontext, internal/testrun, internal/workflow.

Most of these are legitimate (immutable evidence, content-addressed artifact bytes, disposable rebuildable caches, explicitly out-of-scope ceremony per the epic's own boundary, OS lock/token files) but nobody has actually gone through and classified each one as "legitimate exception" vs "should have been migrated." That classification work, plus a generalized architectural test enforcing the resulting allowlist, is the actual full scope of AC4 - not done yet.

## Scope
For each of the ~20 packages above: decide if its file-based persistence is a deliberate, permanent design choice (document why) or a leftover that should move to SQLite. Then write one architectural test (in internal/storage or a new internal/archtest package) enumerating the final allowlist, so any new mutable-metadata file writer added later fails CI until it's either migrated or explicitly added to the allowlist with a reason.

title: internal/search Tokenize has no word-segmentation for scripts without ASCII delimiters (CJK etc.)
description:
## Problem
internal/search/tokenize.go's Tokenize() only splits text on whitespace and a fixed ASCII delimiter set (: / . - _ and camelCase boundaries). Text in a script with no such delimiters - Chinese, Japanese, Korean - never gets split at all: a whole sentence indexes as one opaque FTS token, so any query shorter than the exact full sentence fails to match.

Discovered while adding Unicode regression coverage for punokawan-14yn.15 (Bleve->SQLite FTS5 migration for internal/search). This is NOT a regression from that migration - the old Bleve-backed index used a custom analyzer that wrapped this exact same Tokenize() function, so CJK search was equally broken before. It was simply never covered by a test until now (see internal/search/fts_lifecycle_test.go's TestSearchUnicodeQueryMatchesRecord, which uses whitespace-delimited accented Latin text instead, since that's what the current tokenizer actually supports).

## Scope
Add real word segmentation (or at minimum n-gram/bigram tokenization) for scripts without inherent word boundaries, applied consistently wherever Tokenize's output is stored (internal/search/index.go's ftsValues/tokenizedStream) and where the query itself is tokenized (buildMatchExpr, fuzzyScan).

title: Add a 'latest artifact' projection view for evidence store
description: Follow-up from punokawan-14yn.7. The evidence store (internal/delivery/artifacts.go) currently only supports full enumeration via ListArtifacts (ordered by created_at) - there is no dedicated 'latest artifact for this project/lane/task+kind' query. title: Phase 3 follow-up: ambient work_context_id call-boundary middleware

Deferred because the go-sdk generic AddTool derives each tool's input schema from its Go type, so adding a uniform work_context_id field requires schema injection across ~70 tools; doing it wrong risks breaking existing tools. description: From live-session retro. Gaps: (1) No documented comment-body format contract — Jira Cloud expects Markdown→ADF, not old wiki markup (h3./{{code}} render literally). (3) Ceremony overhead (run_id/requirement_id/task_id/capsule_id) for single-session tasks where durability is never exercised — add optional lightweight mode skipping run/capsule scaffolding for one-off asks. Went well (keep): ingest_jira_requirement, update_jira_task_progress combos, single-approval-per-run, structured plan/assessment persistence.
notes: Concrete native Jira tools requested (currently need raw call_adapter_operation passthrough): (1) search/lookup user (by name/email -> accountId), (2) link issue (create issue link between two keys, e.g. blocks/relates), (3) update story points (custom field, e.g. customfield_100xx — resolve the field id per project). These plus native assign-issue are the common ops that shouldn't require raw passthrough. Each should be approval-gated per the standard external-write model.

title: Implement §11 consistency checks (requires agent judgment, not deterministic code)

The 'consistency checks' bullet list (goals/non-goals don't contradict, delivery phases preserve dependencies, acceptance criteria cover new behavior, removed requirements listed explicitly, new runtime deps declared, security restrictions not weakened without a reviewed comment) all require actual reading comprehension of prose - there is no deterministic heuristic for 'do these two paragraphs contradict.' This either needs an LLM-judged validation step (the revising agent self-reports these, or a separate judge pass) or should be formally scoped out of the plan's acceptance criteria. Filed rather than faked with a heuristic that would produce false confidence.

No such round trip exists today - subagents currently just call punakawan's data tools directly with no capsule-scoped request/response cycle.
close_reason: Shipped internal/contextrequest (fold-latest-per-id JSONL store) plus submit_missing_context_request, list_missing_context_requests, and resolve_missing_context_request MCP tools. Punakawan persists the request/resolution but never chooses between §6.4's four Semar decisions - resolve_missing_context_request just validates added_to_revision names a real capsule (from a prior request_capsule call) and records whichever choice the calling agent made.

title: Implement Semar's knowledge-retrieval-to-capsule pipeline
description: Extract identifiers from the task, run exact+BM25 search, expand one-hop relations, rerank by scope, select within token budget, and build a ContextCapsule recording why each item was included (plan section 15). Depends on AEP-M1 (capsules) and AEP-M6 (search).
notes: Per user decision 2026-07-23: fold stale-knowledge reconciliation into this pipeline. internal/reconcile.CheckSourceStale exists (built in an earlier milestone) but nothing calls it - wire it in here so records get re-checked against their external source right before Semar retrieves them for a capsule, rather than building a separate standalone reconcile tool/scheduler.
close_reason: capsule.BuildFromRetrieval implements the pipeline: search.Search (exact-id+BM25F+fuzzy+one-hop relations, already built in M6), role-based filtering, token-budget selection, and reason-annotated relevant_knowledge. Wired into request_capsule via an optional retrieval_query. Stale-knowledge reconciliation folded in as a lazily-resolved, best-effort ReconcileGate per the 2026-07-23 user decision noted on this issue - no separate standalone reconcile tool was built.

title: Implement knowledge.search MCP tool with ranking and explain-match
description: Wire tokenizer + exact-id detection + alias matching + BM25F + fuzzy fallback + scope/trust/relation-expansion bonuses (plan sections 11.2, 11.9-11.13) into a single search tool that returns match.kind/fields/terms for explainability.
close_reason: Shipped search_knowledge MCP tool: full §11.2 pipeline (BM25F first, fuzzy fallback only on zero hits) plus §11.10's exact-identifier/alias/scope/trust ranking bonuses, §11.9's one-hop relation expansion, and a per-result Explanation for §11.13's explain-match, all returned via match.kind/fields/terms. The tool resyncs the disposable Bleve index (an idempotent full re-upsert via Rebuild) before every query so results are never stale, since no separate refresh_index tool exists yet in this milestone's scope.

title: Implement exact-identifier detection
description: Recognize CVE/GHSA/Sonar-rule/Jira-key/BD-task-id/git-commit-hash/Maven-coordinate/npm-package/PR-number patterns and rank exact identifier matches above every BM25 result (plan section 11.3).
close_reason: internal/search.DetectIdentifiers recognizes CVE/GHSA/Sonar-rule/Jira-key/BD-task-id/PR-number/git-hash/version-string/Maven-coordinate/npm-package/Go-module/file-path/API-route/Java-class-or-method/symbol patterns, ordered most-specific-first so e.g. a Sonar rule (java:S3776) is not mistaken for a generic Maven coordinate. Wired into scoreResult as the +100 exact-identifier bonus that outranks every BM25 result per §11.10.

title: Implement technical tokenizer
description: camelCase/PascalCase/snake_case/kebab-case/dotted-package/colon-coordinate splitting that preserves the original token (plan section 11.6). No aggressive stemming of technical identifiers.
close_reason: internal/search.Tokenize implements the technical tokenizer: splits camelCase/PascalCase/snake_case/kebab-case/dotted-package/colon-coordinate/slash-path tokens while always preserving the original and lowercased whole token, and never splits digits off adjoining letters (java8time stays whole) or explodes acronym runs (URLParser -> URL, Parser not U/R/L/Parser).

title: Integrate Bleve and define BM25F field mappings
description: No search library exists today (confirmed: go.mod has no Bleve/BM25 dependency). Add github.com/blevesearch/bleve and index knowledge_records on title/summary/content/aliases/tags/paths/symbols/identifiers per plan section 11.4-11.5's field weights.
close_reason: Added github.com/blevesearch/bleve/v2, a custom punakawan_technical analyzer backed directly by Tokenize, and internal/search.Index (Open/Close/IndexRecord/DeleteRecord/Rebuild) over §11.4's document model (title/summary/content/aliases/tags/paths/symbols/identifiers, plus type/project/repository/module/trustLevel as keyword fields). §11.5's field weights (identifiers 12.0 down to content 1.0) are applied as per-field query boosts in search.go's BM25F DisjunctionQuery, since Bleve has no static per-field weight on the mapping itself. protocol.KnowledgeRecord gained summary/content/aliases/tags/scope fields to give the document model something to index.

title: Add YAML portable export/import of the knowledge store
description: Plan section 10.1/10.2 calls for a portable.yaml human-readable export that can reconstruct essential knowledge without Dolt. Implement export (Store -> YAML) and import (YAML -> Store) round-trip.
close_reason: Added Store.ExportYAML/ImportYAML (PortableExport{Records}) alongside the existing JSONL Export/Import, giving §10.1's portable.yaml a full round trip through the same Put-based provenance validation as every other write path.

title: Add JSONL knowledge-event export

close_reason: Added .punakawan/events/knowledge-events.jsonl (§10.1/§10.2): Store now emits a put event on every Put and an additional supersede event on every Supersede, readable back via Store.Events() for external tailing/audit.

close_reason: Added superseded_by to protocol.KnowledgeRecord (knowledge.schema.json §10.4) and Store.Supersede(id, supersededBy): marks a record superseded in place via the existing Put path rather than deleting it.

description: internal/adapters.Gate today either succeeds or hard-errors on an adapter write; there is no queued retry or conflict-detection for a Jira sync failure (plan section 9.4/Phase 5). Design a minimal outbound sync queue that records a failed write for retry without blocking BD-side task completion.

New list_jira_sync_queue and retry_jira_sync_entry MCP tools find and replay queued failures. Nothing here blocks or is called by commit_task/finish_task_execution.

Add an EvidenceReference list (or similar) so a TaskContract/GraphResult can enumerate its evidence without relying on path convention alone.
close_reason: Added internal/evidence.Ledger (append-only JSONL of protocol.EvidenceRecord) and RecordArtifact, wired into check_diff/run_tests/check_openapi_compatibility right after each writes its bundle file. title: AEP-M7: Full Semar orchestration over capsules and search
description: Architecture enhancement plan Milestone 7. Depends on AEP-M1 (context capsules) and AEP-M6 (search) landing first - this milestone is Semar's knowledge-retrieval-to-capsule pipeline and the missing-context-request round trip, neither of which can exist before their dependencies. Today the connected MCP client's own model plays every role directly against punakawan's data tools; there is no punakawan-side dispatch of Gareng/Petruk/Bagong as separately constrained invocations.
close_reason: Both AEP-M7 children shipped: Semar's knowledge-retrieval-to-capsule pipeline (m2y, via capsule.BuildFromRetrieval + request_capsule's retrieval_query) and the missing-context-request round trip (uje, via internal/contextrequest + submit/list/resolve_missing_context_request). Semar now has both halves of §6: build a capsule with automatically-retrieved, budget-limited, reason-annotated knowledge, and a way for a subagent to ask for more without searching broadly itself.

title: AEP-M6: Local BM25 knowledge search
description: Architecture enhancement plan Milestone 6. Current state: does not exist at all. go.mod has no search/indexing library (no Bleve; confirmed by grep). internal/knowledge.Store.Get is exact-id lookup only; Store.Related is reverse-relation lookup only, not general search - it is used solely by taskcontext/dossier to populate specific fields, not exposed as a search capability. No tokenizer, no alias matching, no fuzzy fallback, no exact-identifier (CVE/GHSA/Sonar-rule/Jira-key) detection exists anywhere in the codebase.
close_reason: All four AEP-M6 children shipped in internal/search: technical tokenizer (44o), exact-identifier detection (69a), Bleve BM25F integration with §11.5 field weights (6hi), and the search_knowledge MCP tool with full ranking + explain-match (s1z). Local, embeddings-free, no external model calls, per §11.1's search goals. Unblocks AEP-M7 (punokawan-ovm).

title: AEP-M5: Durable knowledge core enhancements
description: Architecture enhancement plan Milestone 5. Current state: internal/knowledge already has Dolt-backed CRUD (Put upserts as revision), relations (Relations/Related), and content-hash staleness detection (internal/reconcile, knowledge.CheckStale/ContentHash). Gaps vs the plan: no supersededBy field or Supersede(id) API on protocol.KnowledgeRecord (records are overwritten in place by Put, with no explicit supersession trail); no JSONL knowledge-event export beyond approvals.jsonl/runs/<run>/events.jsonl; no YAML portable export/import of the knowledge store.
close_reason: All three AEP-M5 children shipped: supersededBy field + Supersede API (pkv), knowledge-events.jsonl audit trail (452), portable YAML export/import (ei9). Durable knowledge core now covers all four §10.1 storage layers (Dolt canonical, JSONL events, YAML portable, BM25 index still pending in AEP-M6).

title: Improve error messages for one-off adapter writes outside the full task-graph pipeline
description: Real-world usage (planning/reviewing Jira ticket TRF-21481 via share-hub) showed that calling call_adapter_operation/update_jira_task_progress directly, without first running the full create_workflow_run -> submit_task_graph -> claim_ready_task -> plan/review pipeline, always fails with "not approved for run" - by design (RequestApproval only creates a pending record; a human must grant it via `punakawan approvals approve`, never another MCP tool). This is correct per the human-in-the-loop model but was not obvious in the moment: the error message does not point at the actual recovery path (punakawan approvals list/approve).

notes: Found while testing the real MCP flow against TRF-21481 in the share-hub repo. Not a bug in the gate itself - the gate behaved correctly - just a discoverability gap.
close_reason: Gate and elicitation fallback errors now include the exact punakawan approvals approve command and approval id. Server instructions, MCP tool descriptions, installer output, and README document inline approval and CLI fallback.
